# What this notebook does

Kate, 2026-10-12: the per-feature SHAP heatmap from `23_shap_gene_clustering.Rmd`, but
clustering **only the `r params$set_word`** (the saved `r params$label` positive set, `r params$set_label`) instead of
all 10,172 modelled genes. `26_target_subtypes_over_time.Rmd` clusters the same genes on the 11
feature families; this one uses the 57 individual features.

- **SHAP is reused, not recomputed.** Each gene's SHAP comes from `23_`'s out-of-fold run: the
  intrinsic regression forest fitted on all genes, with each gene explained by a fold forest
  that never trained on it. The targets are subset *after* explanation - a forest fitted on
  targets alone would have no non-targets to contrast them against.
- **Two profiles:** features normalized within gene (each value / the gene's total |SHAP|, so a
  cluster reflects *which* features drove a gene) and features raw (also how strongly).
- **k** (the number of clusters) is chosen against the column-shuffled null exactly as in `23_`:
  permute each feature independently across genes, standardise the observed silhouette within k,
  then maximise over k. With ~1,400 genes the silhouette is computed on every gene, no sample.
- **Top strips:** cluster and TE change. Whether a gene is also a 4hr / 24hr target is kept in the summary table only.

```{r libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse); library(here); library(cluster); library(pheatmap); library(grid)
})
O <- here("output", "translational_control_overview")
ks <- as.integer(strsplit(params$ks, ",")[[1]])
SAVE <- isTRUE(params$save_plots)
ptag <- sub("_lfc.*$", "", sub("^eif33d_promotes_", "", params$suffix))
K <- as.integer(params$k_report)   # the clustering the summary panels and value heatmaps report
lab_set <- paste(params$label, params$set_word)
stopifnot("report_profile unknown" = params$report_profile %in% c("features, normalized", "features, raw"),
          "k_report must be one of ks" = K %in% ks, "set_rule unknown" = params$set_rule %in% c("knockdown", "relative"))
```

# 1. Targets and their SHAP

```{r load}
f_oof <- file.path(O, paste0("shap_oof_", params$suffix, ".rds"))
stopifnot("out-of-fold SHAP not found - knit 23_shap_gene_clustering.Rmd with this suffix" = file.exists(f_oof))
oof <- readRDS(f_oof)
fc <- colnames(oof$S)
ann <- read_csv(file.path(O, "feature_annotation.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
fam <- setNames(ann$family[match(fc, ann$feature)], fc)
stopifnot("a feature has no family" = !anyNA(fam),
          "SHAP rows and genes out of step" = identical(rownames(oof$S), oof$genes$gene_id_clean))

tg <- oof$genes$set == params$set_label
stopifnot("no genes carry set_label - wrong suffix or label" = sum(tg) > 0)
genes <- oof$genes[tg, ]
S <- oof$S[tg, , drop = FALSE]
# The set must be exactly what its definition and its saved gene-set CSV say.
rule <- if (params$set_rule == "knockdown") {
  # knockdown sets: TE LFC > 0.5 and padj < 0.05
  oof$genes$y > 0.5 & oof$genes$y_padj < 0.05
} else {
  # 10y_sictrl_hypoxia_outcome_prep.R: TE LFC minus the median over modelled genes > 0.5, no padj
  oof$genes$y - median(oof$genes$y) > 0.5
}
gs <- sub("[.].*", "", read_csv(here("output", "genesets", params$geneset_csv), show_col_types = FALSE)$ensembl_gene)
stopifnot("set_label genes do not follow the set's rule" = identical(tg, rule),
          "set_label genes differ from the saved gene-set CSV" = setequal(genes$gene_id_clean, intersect(gs, oof$genes$gene_id_clean)))
cat(sprintf("set '%s': %d genes, matches its rule (%s) and %s\n", params$set_label, sum(tg), params$set_rule, params$geneset_csv))

later <- strsplit(strsplit(params$later_sets, ",")[[1]], "=")
for (s in later) genes[[paste0("target_", s[1])]] <- genes$gene_id_clean %in%
  sub("[.].*", "", read_csv(here("output", "genesets", s[2]), show_col_types = FALSE)$ensembl_gene)
genes$later <- {
  l4 <- genes$target_4hr; l24 <- genes$target_24hr
  case_when(l4 & l24 ~ "4hr and 24hr", l4 ~ "4hr", l24 ~ "24hr", TRUE ~ "1hr only")
}
cat(sprintf("targets %d of %d modelled genes | features %d in %d families\n",
            nrow(genes), nrow(oof$genes), length(fc), n_distinct(fam)))
table(also_target = genes$later)
```

# 2. Two profiles

```{r profiles}
norm_rows <- function(M) M / pmax(rowSums(abs(M)), 1e-12)
profiles <- list(`features, normalized` = norm_rows(S), `features, raw` = S)
stopifnot("normalized rows do not sum to 1 in |SHAP|" = all(abs(rowSums(abs(profiles[[1]])) - 1) < 1e-9))
```

# 3. How many clusters: the null band

```{r null}
sil_of <- function(M, k, seed = 9) {
  set.seed(seed); km <- kmeans(M, centers = k, nstart = 10, iter.max = 50)
  if (length(unique(km$cluster)) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  mean(silhouette(km$cluster, dist(M))[, 3])
}
null_test <- function(M) {
  obs <- vapply(ks, function(k) sil_of(M, k), numeric(1))
  nm <- t(vapply(seq_len(params$n_perm), function(i) {
    set.seed(1000 + i); P <- apply(M, 2, sample)
    vapply(ks, function(k) sil_of(P, k), numeric(1)) }, numeric(length(ks))))
  mu <- colMeans(nm); sdv <- apply(nm, 2, sd)
  stopifnot("null has zero variance" = all(sdv > 0))
  z <- (obs - mu) / sdv
  z_null <- vapply(seq_len(params$n_perm), function(i) { m2 <- nm[-i, , drop = FALSE]
    max((nm[i, ] - colMeans(m2)) / apply(m2, 2, sd)) }, numeric(1))
  list(per_k = tibble(k = ks, observed = obs, null_median = apply(nm, 2, median), null_min = apply(nm, 2, min),
                      null_max = apply(nm, 2, max), z = z),
       p_overall = (sum(z_null >= max(z)) + 1) / (params$n_perm + 1),
       best_k_z = ks[which.max(z)], best_k_sil = ks[which.max(obs)])
}
null_cache <- file.path(O, "shap_oof_cache", sprintf("nulls_targets_%s_perm%d_k%s.rds",
                                                     params$suffix, params$n_perm, gsub(",", "-", params$ks)))
fp <- c(nrow(S), round(sum(abs(S)), 6))
cached <- if (file.exists(null_cache)) readRDS(null_cache) else NULL
nulls <- if (!is.null(cached) && identical(attr(cached, "fingerprint"), fp)) cached else
  structure(map(profiles, null_test), fingerprint = fp)
# the cache predates the US spelling of the profile names; the fingerprint, not the names, says it is current
if (length(nulls) == length(profiles)) names(nulls) <- names(profiles)
if (SAVE && !identical(nulls, cached)) saveRDS(nulls, null_cache)
imap_dfr(nulls, ~ tibble(profile = .y, best_k_sil = .x$best_k_sil, best_k_z = .x$best_k_z,
                         max_z = max(.x$per_k$z), p_overall = .x$p_overall)) %>% knitr::kable(digits = 3)
imap_dfr(nulls, ~ .x$per_k %>% mutate(profile = .y)) %>% knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

```{r fig_null, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.5}
band <- imap_dfr(nulls, ~ .x$per_k %>% mutate(profile = .y))
p_band <- ggplot(band, aes(k)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = null_min, ymax = null_max), fill = "grey85") +
  geom_line(aes(y = null_median), colour = "grey50", linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = observed), colour = "#E69F00", linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(aes(y = observed), colour = "#E69F00") +
  facet_wrap(~ profile, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "number of clusters (k)", y = "mean silhouette score",
       title = sprintf("%s: silhouette score, real vs shuffled SHAP", lab_set),
       subtitle = sprintf("orange = real SHAP; grey band = range over %d shuffles (each feature permuted across genes)\ndashed = shuffled median; n = %d genes",
                          params$n_perm, nrow(genes))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
p_band
if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", paste0("26b_target_shap_features_", ptag, "_null_band.pdf")), p_band, width = 10, height = 4.5)
```

# 4. Heatmaps

Genes are columns, ordered by cluster and, within a cluster, by TE change. Each profile is drawn
at the silhouette peak (`best_k_sil`, the cleanest split) and, if different, at the k best
supported against the null (`best_k_z`). Raw SHAP colors are capped at the 99th percentile of |SHAP|.

```{r heatmaps, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 11, results = "asis"}
# Same family colors as 23_, so the two heatmaps can be read side by side.
fam_cols <- setNames(colorRampPalette(c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2",
                                        "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "grey50"))(n_distinct(fam)), sort(unique(fam)))
sym <- function(x, cap = 1.5) { x <- pmin(pmax(x, -cap), cap); x[c(which.min(x), which.max(x))] <- c(-cap, cap); x }
rows <- fc[order(fam, fc)]
assignments <- list()
for (nm in names(profiles)) for (k in unique(c(nulls[[nm]]$best_k_sil, nulls[[nm]]$best_k_z, K))) {
  M <- profiles[[nm]]
  k_why <- if (k == nulls[[nm]]$best_k_sil) "silhouette peak" else if (k == nulls[[nm]]$best_k_z) "best supported vs null" else "reported k"
  set.seed(9); cl <- kmeans(M, centers = k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 50)$cluster
  cl <- match(cl, as.integer(names(sort(table(cl), decreasing = TRUE))))   # largest = 1
  assignments[[paste(nm, k)]] <- tibble(gene_id_clean = genes$gene_id_clean, symbol = genes$symbol,
                                        profile = nm, k = k, k_choice = k_why, cluster = cl)
  ord <- order(cl, -genes$y)
  H <- t(M[ord, rows, drop = FALSE])
  cap <- if (grepl("raw", nm)) quantile(abs(M), 0.99) else max(abs(M))
  H[H > cap] <- cap; H[H < -cap] <- -cap
  acol <- data.frame(cluster = factor(cl[ord]), lfc = sym(genes$y[ord]),
                     check.names = FALSE, row.names = colnames(H)); names(acol)[2] <- params$lfc_label
  acols <- list(cluster = setNames(c("#0072B2", "#CC79A7", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#D55E00", "#56B4E9", "grey40", "#882255")[seq_len(k)], seq_len(k)),
                lfc_tmp = colorRampPalette(c("#0072B2", "white", "#D55E00"))(51),
                family = fam_cols); names(acols)[names(acols) == "lfc_tmp"] <- params$lfc_label
  hm <- pheatmap::pheatmap(H, cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE, show_colnames = FALSE,
                 color = colorRampPalette(c("#0072B2", "white", "#D55E00"))(101),
                 breaks = seq(-cap, cap, length.out = 102), annotation_col = acol,
                 annotation_row = data.frame(family = fam[rows], row.names = rows),
                 annotation_colors = acols, gaps_col = cumsum(table(cl))[-k], fontsize_row = 6,
                 main = sprintf("%s (n = %d genes)\nper-gene SHAP, %s | k = %d%s\ncolor = %s; orange pushes predicted TE LFC up, blue down (intrinsic regression forest)",
                                lab_set, nrow(genes), nm, k, if (k_why == "silhouette peak") "" else paste0(" (", k_why, ")"),
                                if (grepl("raw", nm)) "SHAP value (TE LFC units)" else "SHAP as share of the gene's total |SHAP|"),
                 fontsize = 9, silent = TRUE)
  cat("\n\n## ", nm, ", k = ", k, "\n\n", sep = ""); grid.newpage(); grid.draw(hm$gtable)
  if (SAVE) {
    f <- here("plots", paste0("26b_target_shap_features_", ptag, "_", gsub("[ ,]+", "_", nm), "_k", k))
    png(paste0(f, ".png"), width = 14, height = 11, units = "in", res = 300); grid.newpage(); grid.draw(hm$gtable); dev.off()
    pdf(paste0(f, ".pdf"), width = 14, height = 11); grid.newpage(); grid.draw(hm$gtable); dev.off()
  }
}
```

# 3b. Silhouette score by number of clusters

The plain version of the section 3 figure: the mean silhouette at each k from 2 to 10, with no
null band. Higher = genes sit more clearly in their own cluster; the peak is the cleanest k.

```{r silhouette_score, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5}
sil_k <- imap_dfr(profiles, ~ tibble(profile = .y, k = 2:10,
                                      silhouette = vapply(2:10, function(k) sil_of(.x, k), numeric(1))))
# k = 2-8 must reproduce the observed values the null test used
for (nm in names(profiles)) stopifnot("silhouette differs from the null-test table" =
  isTRUE(all.equal(sil_k$silhouette[sil_k$profile == nm & sil_k$k <= 8], nulls[[nm]]$per_k$observed)))
knitr::kable(sil_k %>% pivot_wider(names_from = profile, values_from = silhouette), digits = 3)
peak <- sil_k %>% group_by(profile) %>% slice_max(silhouette, n = 1) %>% ungroup()
p_silk <- ggplot(sil_k, aes(k, silhouette)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#E69F00", linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(colour = "#E69F00", size = 2) +
  geom_point(data = peak, shape = 21, size = 4.5, colour = "black", stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = peak, aes(label = sprintf("k = %d\n%.3f", k, silhouette)), vjust = -0.6, size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:10) + scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.2))) +
  facet_wrap(~ profile) +
  labs(x = "number of clusters (k)", y = "mean silhouette score",
       title = sprintf("%s: silhouette score by number of clusters", lab_set),
       subtitle = sprintf("k-means on per-gene SHAP; higher = genes sit more clearly in their own cluster; n = %s genes", scales::comma(nrow(S)))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
p_silk
if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", paste0("26b_target_shap_features_", ptag, "_silhouette_score.pdf")), p_silk, width = 9, height = 4.5)
```

# 4b. How well each gene fits its cluster: silhouette plots and PCA

**Silhouette** for one gene = (b - a) / max(a, b), where a is its mean distance to the other genes
in its own cluster and b its mean distance to the genes of the nearest other cluster. Near 1 =
clearly placed; near 0 = on a boundary; below 0 = closer to another cluster than its own. Each
bar below is one gene, sorted within cluster; the dashed line is the mean, the number used to
pick k. Clusterings are made exactly as for the heatmaps (same seed, largest cluster = 1), so
cluster numbers and colors match.

The PCA puts each gene's SHAP profile on its two main axes of variation, colored by its k = `r params$k_report`
cluster. Overlapping edges are what a mean silhouette of ~0.25 looks like.

```{r silhouette_pca, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5}
cl_cols <- c("#0072B2", "#CC79A7", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#D55E00", "#56B4E9", "grey40", "#882255")
cluster_k <- function(M, k) {
  set.seed(9); cl <- kmeans(M, centers = k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 50)$cluster
  match(cl, as.integer(names(sort(table(cl), decreasing = TRUE))))
}
for (nm in names(profiles)) {
  M <- profiles[[nm]]; D <- dist(M)
  cls <- map(set_names(sort(unique(c(2:4, K)))), ~ cluster_k(M, .x))
  sil <- imap_dfr(cls[as.character(2:4)], ~ tibble(k = as.integer(.y), cluster = factor(.x),
                                width = silhouette(.x, D)[, 3])) %>%
    group_by(k) %>% arrange(cluster, desc(width), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(pos = row_number(), mean_w = mean(width),
           facet = sprintf("k = %d\nmean %.3f, %.1f%% below 0", k[1], mean_w[1], 100 * mean(width < 0))) %>%
    ungroup()
  # the mean must reproduce the silhouette the null test used for this k
  obs <- nulls[[nm]]$per_k
  cat(sprintf("%s: mean silhouette k=2/3/4 here %s | null-test table %s\n", nm,
              paste(sprintf("%.3f", unique(sil$mean_w)), collapse = "/"),
              paste(sprintf("%.3f", obs$observed[obs$k %in% 2:4]), collapse = "/")))
  p_sil <- ggplot(sil, aes(pos, width, fill = cluster)) +
    geom_col(width = 1) +
    geom_hline(aes(yintercept = mean_w), linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +
    coord_flip() + scale_x_reverse() + facet_wrap(~ facet, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cl_cols) +
    labs(x = sprintf("genes, sorted within cluster (n = %s)", scales::comma(nrow(M))), y = "silhouette width",
         title = sprintf("%s, SHAP %s: silhouette of each gene at k = 2, 3, 4", lab_set, nm),
         subtitle = "each bar = one gene; > 0 closer to its own cluster, < 0 closer to another; dashed = mean (the score used to pick k)") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
  print(p_sil)
  pc <- prcomp(M)
  ve <- 100 * pc$sdev^2 / sum(pc$sdev^2)
  pd <- tibble(PC1 = pc$x[, 1], PC2 = pc$x[, 2], cluster = factor(cls[[as.character(K)]]))
  p_pca <- ggplot(pd, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = cluster)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cl_cols) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
    labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%% of variance)", ve[1]), y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%% of variance)", ve[2]),
         title = sprintf("%s\nSHAP %s: PCA, k = %d clusters", lab_set, nm, K),
         subtitle = sprintf("each point = one gene's SHAP profile,\ncolored by its k-means cluster; n = %s genes", scales::comma(nrow(M)))) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
  print(p_pca)
  if (SAVE) {
    tag <- gsub("[ ,]+", "_", nm)
    ggsave(here("plots", paste0("26b_target_shap_features_", ptag, "_", tag, "_silhouette.pdf")), p_sil, width = 11, height = 5)
    ggsave(here("plots", paste0("26b_target_shap_features_", ptag, "_", tag, "_pca_k", K, ".pdf")), p_pca, width = 6.5, height = 5)
  }
}
```

# 4c. Elbow plot

k-means places k centres and assigns each gene to the nearest, moving the centres until the total
squared distance from genes to their centre (within-cluster sum of squares, WSS) stops falling.
WSS always falls as k grows, so the elbow plot shows the **% of total variance explained**
(1 - WSS(k) / WSS(1)) and looks for where the gain per extra cluster drops off. The grey line is
the same curve for column-shuffled SHAP (10 shuffles, the null used in section 3), so the gap
between them is structure that random data with the same feature distributions does not have.

```{r elbow, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.5}
elbow <- imap_dfr(profiles, function(M, nm) {
  wss <- function(X, k) { set.seed(9); kmeans(X, k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 50)$tot.withinss }
  obs <- vapply(1:8, function(k) wss(M, k), numeric(1))
  shuf <- rowMeans(vapply(1:10, function(i) { set.seed(1000 + i); P <- apply(M, 2, sample)
    vapply(1:8, function(k) wss(P, k), numeric(1)) }, numeric(8)))
  tibble(profile = nm, k = 1:8, observed = 100 * (1 - obs / obs[1]), shuffled = 100 * (1 - shuf / shuf[1]))
}) %>% group_by(profile) %>% mutate(gain = observed - lag(observed)) %>% ungroup()
knitr::kable(elbow, digits = 1)
p_elbow <- elbow %>% pivot_longer(c(observed, shuffled), names_to = "data") %>%
  ggplot(aes(k, value, colour = data, linetype = data)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(observed = "#E69F00", shuffled = "grey50"), name = NULL,
                      labels = c(observed = "real SHAP", shuffled = "shuffled SHAP\n(no real groups)")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(observed = 1, shuffled = 2), name = NULL,
                        labels = c(observed = "real SHAP", shuffled = "shuffled SHAP\n(no real groups)")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8) + facet_wrap(~ profile) +
  labs(x = "number of clusters (k)", y = "% of variance explained by clusters",
       title = sprintf("%s: k-means elbow plot", lab_set),
       subtitle = sprintf("bend = where an extra cluster stops adding much; shuffled = mean of 10 shuffles; n = %s genes", scales::comma(nrow(S)))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
p_elbow
if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", paste0("26b_target_shap_features_", ptag, "_elbow.pdf")), p_elbow, width = 10, height = 4.5)
```

# 4c-ii. Elbow plot, pheatmap version (total within-cluster sum of squares)

The same elbow in the form used in the lab's teaching code: k-means run through
`pheatmap(kmeans_k = k)`, k = 2 to 15, and the raw total within-cluster sum of squares (WSS)
plotted instead of % explained. Lower WSS = tighter clusters; look for the bend.

`pheatmap` calls `kmeans(mat, k, iter.max = 100)` with R's default **single random start**,
where section 4c uses 25 starts and keeps the best. One start can settle in a worse solution,
which makes this curve bumpier. The table compares the two at every k; the 25-start WSS is
usually lower, though not guaranteed to be, since the single start is not one of the 25.

```{r elbow_pheatmap, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.5}
wss_ph <- function(knum, x) {
  ph <- pheatmap::pheatmap(mat = x, kmeans_k = knum, scale = "none", cluster_cols = FALSE,
                           clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean", clustering_method = "ward.D2", silent = TRUE)
  ph$kmeans$tot.withinss
}
k2test <- 2:15
elbow_ph <- imap_dfr(profiles, function(M, nm) {
  set.seed(9)
  w1 <- map_vec(k2test, wss_ph, x = M)                                             # pheatmap, 1 start
  w25 <- map_vec(k2test, function(k) { set.seed(9); kmeans(M, k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)$tot.withinss })
  tibble(profile = nm, k = k2test, wss_pheatmap = w1, wss_25_starts = w25)
})
# Best-of-25 is usually but not necessarily lower: pheatmap's single start is not one of the 25.
cat(sprintf("k where the single start beat best-of-25: %s\n",
            paste(elbow_ph$k[elbow_ph$wss_pheatmap < elbow_ph$wss_25_starts - 1e-9], collapse = ", ")))
knitr::kable(elbow_ph %>% mutate(single_start_excess_pct = 100 * (wss_pheatmap / wss_25_starts - 1)), digits = 3)
p_elbow_ph <- ggplot(elbow_ph, aes(k, wss_pheatmap)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = K, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_line(colour = "grey50") + geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k2test) + facet_wrap(~ profile, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "number of clusters K", y = "total within-cluster sum of squares",
       title = sprintf("%s: k-means elbow plot (pheatmap kmeans_k)", lab_set),
       subtitle = sprintf("one k-means start per k, set.seed(9); grey line = reported k; n = %s genes", scales::comma(nrow(S)))) +
  cowplot::theme_cowplot(font_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
p_elbow_ph
if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", paste0("26b_target_shap_features_", ptag, "_elbow_wss_pheatmap.pdf")), p_elbow_ph, width = 10, height = 4.5)
```

# 4d. Dendrogram: an independent clustering method

Hierarchical clustering (Ward's method, Euclidean distance) starts with every gene alone and
repeatedly merges the two groups whose merge adds least within-group variance. The height of each
join is how different the merged groups were, so **a long vertical gap before the next join
means well-separated groups**, and the number of branches crossing that gap is the natural k. The
tree is colored by its own 3-way cut; the bar underneath shows each gene's **k-means** cluster
(heatmap numbering and colors), so agreement between the two methods is visible directly.

```{r dendrogram, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 6}
for (nm in names(profiles)) {
  M <- profiles[[nm]]
  hc <- hclust(dist(M), method = "ward.D2")
  hc3 <- cutree(hc, K)
  km3 <- cluster_k(M, K)
  heights <- rev(hc$height)[1:5]
  cat(sprintf("%s: top join heights %s | hclust k=3 sizes %s | agreement with k-means (ARI) %.2f\n", nm,
              paste(sprintf("%.3f", heights), collapse = ", "), paste(table(hc3), collapse = "/"),
              mclust::adjustedRandIndex(hc3, km3)))
  print(table(hierarchical = hc3, kmeans = km3))
  # color every branch whose leaves all fall in one 3-way-cut group
  tree_cols <- c("#56B4E9", "#D55E00", "#999933", "#332288", "#AA4499", "#44AA99", "#661100", "#888888")[seq_len(K)]   # distinct from the k-means bar colors
  colour_branches <- function(d) {
    lv <- unique(hc3[as.integer(labels(d))])
    col <- if (length(lv) == 1) tree_cols[lv] else "grey30"
    attr(d, "edgePar") <- list(col = col, lwd = 0.6)
    if (!is.leaf(d)) for (i in seq_along(d)) d[[i]] <- colour_branches(d[[i]])
    d
  }
  rownames(M) <- seq_len(nrow(M)); hc$labels <- rownames(M)
  dend <- colour_branches(as.dendrogram(hc))
  draw_dend <- function() {
    layout(matrix(1:2), heights = c(5, 0.6)); par(mar = c(0.5, 7, 4, 1))
    plot(dend, leaflab = "none", ylab = "join height (Ward, Euclidean)",
         main = sprintf("%s, SHAP %s: hierarchical clustering (n = %s genes)",
                        lab_set, nm, scales::comma(nrow(M))), cex.main = 0.95)
    mtext(sprintf("branch color = the tree's own %d-way cut (dashed line); bar below = k-means cluster", K), side = 3, line = 0.4, cex = 0.75)
    abline(h = mean(heights[(K - 1):K]), lty = 2, col = "grey40")
    par(mar = c(1.5, 7, 0, 1))
    ord <- order.dendrogram(dend)
    image(matrix(km3[ord], ncol = 1), col = cl_cols[seq_len(K)], axes = FALSE)
    mtext("k-means cluster", side = 2, las = 1, line = 0.5, cex = 0.8)
    legend("bottom", legend = seq_len(K), fill = cl_cols[seq_len(K)], horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", cex = 0.8, inset = c(0, -0.9), xpd = TRUE)
  }
  draw_dend()
  if (SAVE) { pdf(here("plots", paste0("26b_target_shap_features_", ptag, "_", gsub("[ ,]+", "_", nm), "_dendrogram.pdf")),
                  width = 11, height = 6); draw_dend(); dev.off() }
}
```

# 5. What each cluster is

Per clustering and cluster: size, TE change, the five features with the largest mean |SHAP|
(sign = mean direction), and the cluster's median sequence values, so a group reads as e.g.
"GC-rich, short CDS" rather than only as SHAP colors.

```{r cluster_summary}
fm <- readRDS(file.path(O, params$matrix_rds))
seqv <- fm %>% transmute(gene_id_clean, cds_gc, gc3 = gc3_internal, cds_nt = 2^log2_cds_length - 1,
                         utr5_nt = 2^log2_utr5_length - 1, utr5_access = tco_struct_accessibility_utr5_mean) %>%
  distinct(gene_id_clean, .keep_all = TRUE)
all_assign <- bind_rows(assignments) %>%
  left_join(genes %>% dplyr::select(gene_id_clean, y, pred_oof, later), by = "gene_id_clean")
shap_long <- as_tibble(S, rownames = "gene_id_clean") %>% pivot_longer(-gene_id_clean, names_to = "feature", values_to = "shap")
top_feat <- all_assign %>% dplyr::select(profile, k, cluster, gene_id_clean) %>%
  inner_join(shap_long, by = "gene_id_clean", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  group_by(profile, k, cluster, feature) %>% summarise(m = mean(shap), a = mean(abs(shap)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(profile, k, cluster) %>% slice_max(a, n = 5) %>%
  summarise(top_features = paste0(feature, ifelse(m > 0, " (+)", " (-)"), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")
summ <- all_assign %>% left_join(seqv, by = "gene_id_clean") %>% group_by(profile, k, cluster) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), median_lfc = median(y), median_pred = median(pred_oof),
            also_4hr_or_24hr = sum(later != "1hr only"),
            cds_gc = median(cds_gc, na.rm = TRUE), gc3 = median(gc3, na.rm = TRUE), cds_nt = median(cds_nt, na.rm = TRUE),
            utr5_nt = median(utr5_nt, na.rm = TRUE), utr5_access = median(utr5_access, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(top_feat, by = c("profile", "k", "cluster"))
stopifnot("every target must be in every clustering" = all(dplyr::count(all_assign, profile, k)$n == nrow(genes)))
knitr::kable(summ, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 3, 0))
if (SAVE) {
  write_csv(all_assign, file.path(O, paste0("target_shap_feature_clusters_", params$suffix, ".csv")))
  write_csv(summ, file.path(O, paste0("target_shap_feature_cluster_summary_", params$suffix, ".csv")))
}
```

# 6. The features themselves: correlation with TE change, and mean value per cluster

Same 57 rows, in the same order and with the same family bar as the heatmaps above, for the
**`r params$report_profile` k = `r params$k_report`** clustering (`k_report`; hypoxia 1hr: Kate, 2026-10-12, stick with three). Feature values come
unimputed from the matrix; each cell uses the genes that have a value.

- **Left - correlation with TE change:** Spearman rho between the feature's value and
  log2(sictrl / si3d) TE change. The first column is every modelled gene; the rest are within the
  targets. Within targets the TE change is already truncated at > 0.5, so those correlations are
  weaker by construction and answer a different question (which features track *how strongly* a
  target depends on eIF3d).
- **Right - mean value:** each group's mean expressed as a z-score against all modelled genes
  ((group mean - all-gene mean) / all-gene sd), so features on different scales share one color
  bar. Orange = higher than a typical modelled gene, blue = lower. Raw means are in the CSV.

```{r feature_panels, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 11}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(ComplexHeatmap); library(circlize) })
cl3 <- assignments[[paste(params$report_profile, K)]]
stopifnot("report_profile k = K clustering missing" = !is.null(cl3), identical(cl3$gene_id_clean, genes$gene_id_clean))
Xall <- fm[match(oof$genes$gene_id_clean, fm$gene_id_clean), fc] %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(unlist(.x)))) %>% as.matrix()
stopifnot("modelled genes missing from the matrix" = !anyNA(match(oof$genes$gene_id_clean, fm$gene_id_clean)))
yall <- oof$genes$y
grp <- list(all = rep(TRUE, nrow(oof$genes)), targets = tg)
for (g in seq_len(K)) grp[[paste("cluster", g)]] <- oof$genes$gene_id_clean %in% cl3$gene_id_clean[cl3$cluster == g]
n_of <- map_int(grp, sum)
lab <- c(all = sprintf("all modelled genes\n(n = %s)", format(n_of[["all"]], big.mark = ",")),
         targets = sprintf("all targets\n(n = %s)", format(n_of[["targets"]], big.mark = ",")),
         setNames(sprintf("cluster %d\n(n = %d)", seq_len(K), n_of[paste("cluster", seq_len(K))]), paste("cluster", seq_len(K))))

rho <- sapply(grp, function(w) apply(Xall[w, rows, drop = FALSE], 2, function(x)
  if (sum(!is.na(x)) < 10 || sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) == 0) NA_real_ else cor(x, yall[w], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")))
mu_all <- colMeans(Xall[, rows], na.rm = TRUE); sd_all <- apply(Xall[, rows], 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
raw_mean <- sapply(grp[-1], function(w) colMeans(Xall[w, rows, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
zmean <- (raw_mean - mu_all) / ifelse(sd_all > 0, sd_all, NA)
stopifnot("correlation outside [-1, 1]" = all(abs(rho) <= 1, na.rm = TRUE),
          "group means not finite" = all(is.finite(raw_mean[sd_all > 0, ])))
colnames(rho) <- lab[colnames(rho)]; colnames(zmean) <- lab[colnames(zmean)]

fam_ha <- rowAnnotation(family = fam[rows], col = list(family = fam_cols), show_annotation_name = FALSE)
cell_txt <- function(M) function(j, i, x, y, w, h, fill)
  if (!is.na(M[i, j])) grid.text(sprintf("%.2f", M[i, j]), x, y, gp = gpar(fontsize = 5.5, col = "grey20"))
rcap <- max(abs(rho), na.rm = TRUE); zcap <- quantile(abs(zmean), 0.98, na.rm = TRUE)
# Two separate figures, each with its own family bar and feature names.
panel <- function(M, cap, legend, title, subtitle) {
  ht <- Heatmap(M, name = legend, left_annotation = fam_ha,
                col = colorRamp2(c(-cap, 0, cap), c("#0072B2", "white", "#D55E00")), na_col = "grey85",
                cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_columns = FALSE, row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6.5),
                column_names_rot = 45, column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8), cell_fun = cell_txt(M),
                column_title = subtitle, column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10))
  list(ht = ht, title = sprintf("%s, %s SHAP k = %d\n%s", lab_set, sub("features, ", "", params$report_profile), K, title))
}
panels <- list(
  cor = panel(rho, rcap, "Spearman rho\nwith TE change", "correlation of each feature with TE change",
              paste("Spearman rho with", sub(" [(]cap 1.5[)]", "", params$lfc_label))),
  mean = panel(zmean, zcap, "mean value\n(z vs all genes)", "mean feature value per cluster",
               "z-score vs all modelled genes: (group mean - all-gene mean) / all-gene sd"))
draw_panel <- function(p) draw(p$ht, column_title = p$title, merge_legend = TRUE,
                               column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 11, fontface = "bold"))
for (p in panels) draw_panel(p)
if (SAVE) {
  for (nm in names(panels)) {
    f <- here("plots", paste0("26b_target_feature_", nm, "_", ptag, "_k", K))
    w <- if (nm == "cor") 8.5 else 8
    pdf(paste0(f, ".pdf"), width = w, height = 11); draw_panel(panels[[nm]]); dev.off()
    png(paste0(f, ".png"), width = w, height = 11, units = "in", res = 300); draw_panel(panels[[nm]]); dev.off()
  }
  write_csv(tibble(feature = rows, family = fam[rows]) %>%
              bind_cols(as_tibble(setNames(as.data.frame(rho), paste0("rho_", names(grp))))) %>%
              bind_cols(as_tibble(setNames(as.data.frame(raw_mean), paste0("mean_", names(grp)[-1])))) %>%
              mutate(mean_all = mu_all, sd_all = sd_all) %>%
              bind_cols(as_tibble(setNames(as.data.frame(zmean), paste0("z_", names(grp)[-1])))),
            file.path(O, paste0("target_feature_cor_and_mean_", params$suffix, ".csv")))
}
```

# 6b. Feature values per gene, in the SHAP heatmap layout

The section 4 heatmaps with each cell colored by the gene's own **feature value** instead of its
SHAP value: same genes, same column order (cluster, then TE change), same rows and annotations,
so the two can be laid side by side. Values are z-scores against all modelled genes, the
per-gene version of the mean-value panel above; capped at +/-2.5, missing values grey.
Correlation has no per-gene version (it needs a group of genes), so it stays a summary panel.

```{r value_heatmaps, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 11, results = "asis"}
Zall <- sweep(sweep(Xall[, rows], 2, mu_all), 2, ifelse(sd_all > 0, sd_all, NA), "/")
Ztg <- Zall[match(genes$gene_id_clean, oof$genes$gene_id_clean), , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot("target rows out of step" = identical(oof$genes$gene_id_clean[match(genes$gene_id_clean, oof$genes$gene_id_clean)], genes$gene_id_clean))
# Soundness: the values shown are the ones the forest saw, and the per-gene z-scores reproduce
# the summary mean panel. Model data are imputed, so only the matrix's non-missing cells compare.
md_chk <- readRDS(file.path(O, paste0("rfreg_model_data_", params$suffix, ".rds")))
mg <- bind_rows(md_chk$train, md_chk$test)
Xm <- as.matrix(mg[match(oof$genes$gene_id_clean, mg$gene_id_clean), rows])
stopifnot("heatmap features are not the model's" = setequal(rows, md_chk$feature_cols),
          "heatmap genes are not the model's" = setequal(oof$genes$gene_id_clean, mg$gene_id_clean),
          "matrix values differ from the model data" = max(abs((Xall[, rows] - Xm)[!is.na(Xall[, rows])])) < 1e-9,
          "matrix has duplicate genes" = !anyDuplicated(fm$gene_id_clean),
          "z-scores not centred / scaled" = max(abs(colMeans(Zall, na.rm = TRUE)), na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-9,
          "per-gene cluster means do not reproduce the mean panel" =
            max(abs(sapply(seq_len(K), function(g) colMeans(Ztg[cl3$cluster == g, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)) -
                    zmean[, paste0("cluster ", seq_len(K), "\n(n = ", n_of[paste("cluster", seq_len(K))], ")")]), na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-9,
          # alignment: a feature's SHAP must track its own value (sign depends on the contrast)
          "cds_gc SHAP does not track cds_gc value - rows misaligned" = abs(cor(Ztg[, "cds_gc"], S[, "cds_gc"], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")) > 0.5)
cat(sprintf("matrix cells missing (grey; imputed inside the model): %d of %d\n", sum(is.na(Xall[, rows])), length(Xall[, rows])))
zc <- 2.5
for (nm in names(profiles)) {
  a <- assignments[[paste(nm, K)]]
  stopifnot("k = K clustering missing" = !is.null(a), identical(a$gene_id_clean, genes$gene_id_clean))
  cl <- a$cluster
  ord <- order(cl, -genes$y)
  H <- t(Ztg[ord, , drop = FALSE]); colnames(H) <- genes$gene_id_clean[ord]
  H[H > zc] <- zc; H[H < -zc] <- -zc
  acol <- data.frame(cluster = factor(cl[ord]), lfc = sym(genes$y[ord]),
                     check.names = FALSE, row.names = colnames(H)); names(acol)[2] <- params$lfc_label
  acols <- list(cluster = setNames(cl_cols[seq_len(K)], seq_len(K)),
                lfc_tmp = colorRampPalette(c("#0072B2", "white", "#D55E00"))(51),
                family = fam_cols); names(acols)[names(acols) == "lfc_tmp"] <- params$lfc_label
  # ComplexHeatmap (loaded in section 6) masks pheatmap(); call the original
  hm <- pheatmap::pheatmap(H, cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE, show_colnames = FALSE,
                 color = colorRampPalette(c("#0072B2", "white", "#D55E00"))(101),
                 breaks = seq(-zc, zc, length.out = 102), na_col = "grey85", annotation_col = acol,
                 annotation_row = data.frame(family = fam[rows], row.names = rows),
                 annotation_colors = acols, gaps_col = cumsum(table(cl))[-K], fontsize_row = 6,
                 main = sprintf("%s (n = %d genes)\nper-gene feature values, genes grouped by %s SHAP clusters | k = %d\ncolor = z-score vs all modelled genes (orange higher, blue lower, capped at +/-2.5); grey = missing",
                                lab_set, nrow(genes), sub("features, ", "", nm), K), fontsize = 9, silent = TRUE)
  cat("\n\n## ", nm, ", feature values\n\n", sep = ""); grid.newpage(); grid.draw(hm$gtable)
  if (SAVE) {
    f <- here("plots", paste0("26b_target_feature_values_", ptag, "_", gsub("[ ,]+", "_", nm), "_k", K))
    png(paste0(f, ".png"), width = 14, height = 11, units = "in", res = 300); grid.newpage(); grid.draw(hm$gtable); dev.off()
    pdf(paste0(f, ".pdf"), width = 14, height = 11); grid.newpage(); grid.draw(hm$gtable); dev.off()
  }
}
```
